subject: Food Science
title: Anatomy of an Outbreak
description: A 60-second lesson on Anatomy of an Outbreak.

hook.text: In 2018, romaine lettuce sickened 210 people across 36 states. Tracing the source took 3 weeks and hundreds of investigators.

buildup.text: Outbreaks start with clusters: multiple people sick with the same pathogen in the same time frame, reported to authorities.

discovery.text: PulseNet matches DNA fingerprints of pathogens from patients nationwide—connecting cases that seem unrelated.

twist.text: Most outbreaks are never detected. If the pathogen isn't reported or tested, the cases look like random stomach bugs.

climax.text: Epidemiologists interview patients about what they ate, where they shopped, and when—building a statistical case for the source.

punchline.text: DNA matching, interviews, supply chain tracing. Outbreak investigation is detective work.

quiz.question: What does PulseNet do in outbreak investigations?
options: Matches pathogen DNA fingerprints from patients across the country
